clue.text: See if the underground's working in the lab

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the vessel rather than a strict noun synonym

blocks.note: to see if something works is to test it
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether the Underground is running, oddly from inside a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the everyday name for the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass cylinder closed at one end is standard chemistry apparatus, constantly in use at the bench.

clue.text: A front for religion?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cover organisation pretending to be a church
setter's reading: a part at the front side of the head that shares its name with a house of worship

explanation.walkthrough: A 'front' suggests a sham organisation, but the clue means a building for religion that is also a part of the head beside the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a building for worship and the flat area at each side of the forehead.

clue.text: Keep protecting silver from barbarian

indicators.note: to protect something is to wrap around it, so one word sits round the other

blocks.note: to keep is to save
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Guarding the family silver from a marauding invader.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a wild, uncivilised, brutal person, used as nouns here.

clue.text: Don't keep a secret and don't be enclosed at end of ring

indicators.note: something enclosed is shut inside another thing, so these words go within the first

blocks.note: to tell is to give a secret away
'and don't be' can be phrased 'nor be'

explanation.surface: Advice to blab and refuse to be confined, as the bell-ringing finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: TELL goes round NOR BE. In church bell-ringing a ring is a set of bells, and the deepest bell rings last in each round.
explanation.definitionFit: In change ringing, the heaviest and lowest bell of a set usually sounds last, closing each sequence.

clue.text: Live to see the sea seethe less than usual?

blocks.note: to live is to be, to exist
lo is an old word meaning look, see
the waves stand for the sea
to seethe is to rage

explanation.surface: A seaside instruction: live long enough to watch the ocean churn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poorer or smaller than the norm falls under the typical level, an adjectival phrase here.

clue.text: Secret police's 26

definitions.note: a cross-reference: 26 across is ARREST, used as a noun meaning a halt

blocks.note: the Stasi were the East German secret police
the possessive ending taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Look up 26 across: its answer, ARREST, read as a noun meaning a stoppage, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of inactivity or stoppage, just as an arrest of growth or movement is a halt.

clue.text: There's too much French about love for soldiers

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: trop is French for too much
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A complaint that the French overdo romance with men in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of cavalry or a body of soldiers in general is called by this collective noun.

clue.text: Provocative person canonised criminal Jack

blocks.note: a canonised person is a saint, abbreviated St
Jack the Ripper, the Victorian London murderer

explanation.surface: A shocking figure who made a saint of a notorious killer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who removes clothes as an erotic performance is deliberately titillating, a playful description.

clue.text: Most worshippers at 1 down (19 heaven) I enabled to fly

definitions.note: the answer speaks in the first person: the helicopter pioneer

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter is kept

blocks.note: 1 down and 19 make the Golden Temple at Amritsar, holiest shrine of one faith
19 is golden, and or is gold in heraldry
heaven is the sky

explanation.surface: An aviator boasting that most pilgrims at a famous shrine were given wings by him.
explanation.walkthrough: The 19 does double duty: with 1 down it gives the Golden Temple, and alone it gives OR. Igor Sikorsky built the first practical helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Sikorsky designed early aircraft and the first mass-produced helicopter, so the engineer let people take flight.

clue.text: Magic herb holding most of French score so as to stir one's emotions

definitions.text: so as to stir one's emotions

indicators.note: most of a word keeps all but its last letter
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one word goes in the other

blocks.note: moly is the magic herb Hermes gives Odysseus in Homer
vingt is French for twenty, a score

explanation.surface: A spell-casting plant clutching a French sum, to touch the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb describing an action done in a touching way, one that rouses deep feelings.

clue.text: Heard to tolerate North African port

indicators.note: heard tells us to go by how the words sound when spoken

blocks.note: to brook is to tolerate

explanation.surface: Someone overheard putting up with a coastal town in Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: The Libyan harbour town was besieged in the Second World War and sits on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Revealing bad turn onto motorway by one locally born

blocks.note: ill means bad
a U-turn
M for motorway, as in the M1
I is the Roman numeral one
a native is someone born in the place

explanation.surface: A local resident's ill-advised U-turn on a motorway exposes something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that throws light on a subject enlightens or makes it clear, an adjective in both.

clue.text: Drunks that are dis-orderly - result goal

indicators.note: the hyphen stresses 'out of order', so the letters lose their sequence

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Rowdy football fans celebrating a win and a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorderly' also describes the drunks, but the hyphen marks it as the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Young men who behave rowdily after heavy beer drinking are inebriated people, plural in both.

clue.text: Background music to be cut to size?

blocks.note: first meaning: bland music nobody really listens to
second meaning: decorative paper trimmed into lengths to hang on walls

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint rather than a synonym: rolls of decorative paper are trimmed to fit the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unobtrusive music played as background, and decorative paper pasted onto interior walls.

clue.text: Sufferer from severe stress over Sun disclosing Western concern

indicators.note: read as dis-closing, the letters are opened up and lose their arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
W for western
reck is an old word for heed or concern

explanation.surface: A stressed-out tabloid reporter revealing worries about the West.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is loose: 'disclosing' must be read as opening up the letters of 'over Sun'. The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a state of extreme anxiety and agitation is described informally with this phrase.

clue.text: Instrument for East Anglian water table

blocks.note: the Wash is a large bay on the coast of East Anglia
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A tool for measuring the water level in eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water table' looks like one hydrological term, but it splits. East Anglia is the eastern bulge of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridged laundry board is scraped with thimbles as a percussion device in skiffle and jug bands.

clue.text: A short row before breeze gets up in Cumbria

definitions.note: names the town by its location

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a spat is a brief quarrel
a breeze is a movement of air

explanation.surface: A brief argument just before the wind rises in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumbria is a county in north-west England; Aspatria is a small town there.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a small market town in the north-west English county, so it is located there.

clue.text: If the Queen take (the responsibility)

blocks.note: 'should you need help' means 'if you need help'
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A conditional royal instruction about accepting the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a burden or accept a duty is to carry it as if on your upper body, a verb.

clue.text: Harpy's logic's used by learned traveller

indicators.note: letters that are used are put to work in some new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A shrewish woman's reasoning exploited by a well-read wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scholar-Gipsy is Matthew Arnold's poem about an Oxford student who left to wander with travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold's title figure is an educated man who abandoned university to roam the countryside with nomads.

clue.text: Prosperous chancellor after holiday in the sun?

blocks.note: golden means prosperous, as in a golden age
Gordon Brown, Chancellor of the Exchequer when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A well-off finance minister relaxing on a sunny break.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was the UK's Chancellor of the Exchequer, its finance minister, from 1997 to 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: A suntanned complexion after a beach trip is a warm tan colour, an adjective describing skin.

clue.text: Catalyst for solvers raised outside New Zealand and setter

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a word reads it from the bottom up
outside means the word goes around the next one

blocks.note: ye is the old plural you, addressing the solvers
NZ is the abbreviation for New Zealand
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A trigger for crossword fans brought up abroad, along with the compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: A protein that speeds up a biochemical reaction without being consumed is a biological accelerator.

clue.text: Dove-like plant, the second to surround walker in water

indicators.note: surrounding something means going around it on all sides
in places the preceding letters inside the following word

blocks.note: II is the Roman numeral two, as in Elizabeth II
a leg is what one walks with
aqua is Latin for water

explanation.surface: A garden plant described as like a dove, with something wading in water.
explanation.walkthrough: Aquilegia is the columbine, whose common name comes from the Latin for dove; its Latin name, oddly, means eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: The columbine flower's petals were thought to resemble a cluster of doves, giving it its name.

clue.text: See 12
See 19
Bone from the centre?

definitions.note: a hint at a line from the centre, not a strict noun

blocks.note: first meaning: the forearm bone on the thumb side
second meaning: a straight line from the middle of a circle to its edge

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is hinted rather than defined: the line runs from the centre of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: It names one of the two forearm bones and, in geometry, the distance from a circle's middle to its circumference.

clue.text: Reptile beheaded amid distorted magic

indicators.note: beheading a word cuts off its first letter
amid means in the middle of, so it goes inside the next word

blocks.note: a lizard is a reptile
wry means twisted or distorted

explanation.surface: A decapitated reptile lying among twisted sorcery.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery and enchantment are the arts of a wizard, so the nouns share the sense of supernatural power.

clue.text: Stop and have a breather, do you hear?

indicators.note: do you hear asks us to go by the spoken sound of the words

blocks.note: a breather is a rest

explanation.surface: Someone told to halt and catch their breath, with a nudge to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or check something, as in arresting decline, is to bring it to a standstill, a verb.

clue.text: Instead, ancestral afternoon entertainment is provided

indicators.note: the phrase is provided by the words before it, which contain it whole

blocks.note: letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An ancestral pastime offered as a replacement for something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A social gathering with dancing held in the late afternoon, with refreshments, is a daytime amusement.
